title: Guidance API entry
description: Schema for one guidance-api/<id>.json file. See guidance-api/README.md for the full rationale (why this is a separate API from component-api), this file is the machine-checkable version of that same schema.

id.description: Must match the id used for the same component in component-api exactly, this is the join key. Not a tag name: some entries (like toolbox) have no real custom element behind them at all.

dos.description: Things to do. May be empty. Not padded to hit a count, if only one real thing is worth saying, there's one entry.

donts.description: Things to avoid, ideally naming the concrete symptom of getting it wrong, not just "don't do X".

behavior.description: Optional. Neutral facts about how the component actually behaves at runtime (what triggers a state change, what real element or event backs an interaction, what condition picks between two real implementations). Often the single most load-bearing fact about the component, sometimes already stated quietly in an attribute or event's own description elsewhere in component-api, surfaced here in one obvious place the same way dos/donts already restate a real fact for emphasis. Not advice: a dos/donts entry says what to do about a fact, a behavior entry just states the fact. May be absent entirely; most entries won't have one yet.

configuration.description: Optional. Static facts about which props/attributes/slots are only meaningful together, mutually exclusive, or gate one another, a discriminated union in the component's own API surface. Different axis from behavior: behavior is about WHEN something happens at runtime, configuration is about which combination of props is even valid or renders differently in the first place (card.expanded only means anything when type="accordion"; a component's supportPage attribute and its support-link slot are mutually gated). Not a restatement of token-api's own layout/spacing values, this is about the component's API shape, not its visual spacing. May be absent entirely; most entries won't have one yet.

reference.description: Optional, and categorically different from every other field here: an external, industry-convention fact (a named UX pattern, an established design system's own guidance for the equivalent control), not a verified fact about Firefox's own real implementation. Every other field in this schema is grounded in someone having read Firefox's actual source; a reference entry is grounded in a real, cited, external document instead, and must never be phrased as if it describes what Firefox's code does. Each entry requires a real source URL, unlike dos/donts/behavior/configuration where the citation lives inline in the prose. Used sparingly, only where a genuinely well-established, specifically-relevant convention exists (an accessibility interaction pattern from the W3C ARIA Authoring Practices Guide, another real design system's own written guidance for the equivalent control), not generic blog-post UX advice.

text.description: One sentence, citing something concrete and specific to this component's real implementation (a method, property, or lifecycle behavior), not generic UX advice.
The external convention or guidance, stated as belonging to that source, not as a fact about Firefox's own implementation.

source.description: A real, specific URL to the document this is quoting or paraphrasing. Required, this is the only field in the schema whose factual basis is unverifiable without it.
